task.goal: A gateway enforces max_requests per tenant in a rolling time window. It currently uses one global timestamp list and drops requests exactly at the window boundary incorrectly. Fix RateLimiter.allow(tenant, now) in limiter.py. Each tenant has its own limit; requests older than or exactly window seconds expire; denied requests must not consume quota; reject nonpositive limits/windows. Run visible tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace.My assertion at now=2 was wrong (stamps 0 and 1 are still within the 10s window, so it should deny). Fixing the check and re-running.Fixed `RateLimiter` in limiter.py:

- Per-tenant timestamp lists (`self.timestamps` is now a dict keyed by tenant) instead of one global list, so each tenant has its own quota.
- Expiry uses `now - stamp < self.window`, so a request exactly `window` seconds old expires (previously `<=` kept it).
- Denied requests no longer consume quota — the filtered list is only written back, and timestamps are appended only on allow.
- `__init__` raises `ValueError` for nonpositive `max_requests` or `window`.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest -v test_limiter` passes (both visible tests), plus targeted checks for the exact-window boundary, expiry freeing quota, repeated denials not consuming slots, tenant isolation, and rejection of nonpositive limits/windows — all pass under requirement "visible tests and boundary/quota/validation checks pass".
